items.prompt: How do you say "good morning" in Italian?
rubric: Buongiorno is the standard daytime greeting.
Buonanotte (good night) and Buonasera (good evening) are tied to other times of day; Arrivederci means goodbye.

items.prompt: Which Italian word means "thank you"?
rubric: Grazie means thank you.
Prego (you're welcome) is the reply to grazie and is often confused with it; Scusi means excuse me; Per favore means please.

items.prompt: Which form of the verb essere (to be) goes with the pronoun io?
rubric: Io sono means I am.
Sei is for tu, è for lui/lei, and siamo for noi.

items.prompt: Which definite article goes before the masculine singular noun libro (book)?
rubric: Il libro is the correct masculine singular form.
La is feminine singular; i and le are plural.

items.prompt: What number is otto?
rubric: Otto is eight.
Learners often mix it up with sette (7) or nove (9).

items.prompt: Which of these are days of the week in Italian? Select all that apply.
rubric: Lunedì, martedì and giovedì are Monday, Tuesday and Thursday.
Gennaio (January) and marzo (March) are months, a frequent mix-up.

items.prompt: You are invited to dinner and meet your friend's elderly grandmother for the first time. Your teacher told you that Italians use a polite form of address with people they do not know well or who are older. Which pronoun is the formal singular "you" in Italian?
rubric: Lei is the formal singular you.
Tu is informal singular; voi is plural you; loro means they.

items.prompt: Which sentence correctly means "The girls are tall"?
rubric: Article, noun, verb and adjective all agree in feminine plural.
The distractors break number or gender agreement.

items.prompt: Which of these Italian nouns is feminine?
rubric: Nouns ending in -a are usually feminine, so casa is feminine.
Libro, zaino and amico end in -o and are masculine.

items.prompt: How are the letters "ci" pronounced in the word ciao?

options.label: Like "k" in kite, as in cane
Like "s" in sun, as in city
Like "sh" in shoe, as in chef

rubric: Before i and e, c is pronounced like English ch.
The k sound is for c before a, o, u, or ch before i/e.

items.prompt: What does the sentence "Non ho fame" mean?
rubric: Avere fame (to have hunger) expresses being hungry; non negates it.
The distractors mistake fame for similar-sounding or related ideas.

items.prompt: Why can an Italian speaker say just "Mangio una mela" without the pronoun io?

options.label: The word mela shows the speaker is the subject
The verb ending -o already shows the subject is io
Italian never uses subject pronouns in any sentence
Pronouns are dropped only when the verb is past tense

rubric: Verb endings carry person information, so the subject pronoun is optional.
Pronouns are not banned; they are used for emphasis or contrast.

items.prompt: Which of these noun phrases use the correct definite article? Select all that apply.
rubric: L'amico (vowel) and lo zaino (z) are correct.
Il studente should be lo studente (s + consonant); la amica should be l'amica.

items.prompt: You are visiting Rome and want to buy bread at a small bakery. On the door you see a sign: "Chiuso la domenica". You are planning your week and want to know what the sign tells you. What does it mean?

options.label: The shop is closed on Sundays
The shop is closed today for a holiday
The shop is closed on Mondays
The shop is open on Sundays

rubric: Chiuso means closed and la domenica means on Sundays as a habit.
Learners may confuse chiuso with aperto (open) or misread the day.

items.prompt: Why does Italian say "Maria è partita" instead of "Maria ha partito" in the passato prossimo?

options.label: Partire is a transitive verb, so it takes essere and agrees with the direct object
Partire is an irregular verb, so it takes avere only when the subject is male
Partire is a reflexive verb, so it takes essere and the participle stays masculine
Partire is a verb of movement, so it takes essere and the participle agrees with Maria

rubric: Verbs of movement like partire take essere, and the participle agrees with the subject.
Distractors confuse the rule with reflexive, irregular or transitive verb behaviour.

items.prompt: In which situation would an Italian speaker normally use the formal pronoun Lei?

options.label: Chatting with a new classmate of your own age at university
Asking an older stranger for directions
Greeting your younger cousin when you arrive at a party
Texting your best friend about plans for the weekend

rubric: Lei is used with strangers, elders and formal contacts.
Distractors are informal settings where tu is normal.

items.prompt: Which word begins with a hard "k" sound?
rubric: Before i or e, "ch" is pronounced /k/, so chi starts with a hard k.
Ce and ci are pronounced like English "ch"; learners mistake these for the hard sound.

items.prompt: How does an Italian say that they themselves feel cold?
rubric: Italian uses avere for physical sensations such as cold, hunger and thirst.
Sono freddo is the English-style calque and would mean you are a cold person.

items.prompt: Why do Italians say "lo zaino" rather than "il zaino"?

options.label: Lo is used before masculine nouns that name things rather than people or animals
Lo is used before any masculine noun that ends in the letter o, as opposed to e
Lo is used before masculine nouns starting with z, gn, ps or s plus a consonant
Lo is used before masculine nouns that begin with a vowel sound, as in lo amico

rubric: Lo replaces il before z, gn, ps and s+consonant.
Distractors invent rules based on endings, meaning or vowels (l' is used before vowels).

items.prompt: Which of these Italian plurals are correct? Select all that apply.
rubric: Hard c and g sounds are kept with h in the plural, and accented nouns stay unchanged.
Uomo has the irregular plural uomini, so uomi is wrong.

items.prompt: You read this text message from an Italian acquaintance: "Ieri sono stata al mare con Luca." You know nothing else about the writer. What does the sentence tell you?

options.label: The writer is female, because the participle stata agrees with the subject
Luca is female, because stata agrees with the person mentioned last
The writer is plural, because the auxiliary sono is a plural form
The writer is speaking formally, because sono is the polite form of the verb

rubric: With essere the participle agrees with the subject, so stata signals a female writer.
Distractors misread sono as formal or plural, or attach agreement to Luca.

items.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Noi ___ italiano con i nostri amici." (parlare, present)
rubric: Noi takes the ending -iamo for -are verbs: parliamo.
Other options are the io, voi and loro forms.

items.prompt: A woman says she went to the cinema yesterday. Which sentence is correct?
rubric: Andare takes essere, and the participle agrees with a female subject: andata.
Distractors use avere or the masculine participle.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: "Domani vado ___ supermercato."
rubric: A + il combines to al to express going to a place.
Nel means in the, and dal means from the or to someone's place.

items.prompt: Replace the object with a pronoun: "Vedo Marco ogni giorno."
rubric: Marco is a masculine direct object, so lo goes before the verb.
Gli is an indirect pronoun, la is feminine, and the pronoun cannot follow a conjugated verb.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: "Questa è ___ madre, si chiama Giulia." (speaker's own mother)
rubric: Possessives with singular family members drop the article: mia madre.
La mia madre keeps the article, which is the common error; la sua refers to someone else.

items.prompt: Which of these sentences are grammatically correct? Select all that apply.
You are emailing your Italian teacher, whom you address formally, to ask when the exam starts. You want a polite, correct opening question. Which one fits?

options.label: Può dirti a che ora inizia l'esame?
Potete dirmi a che ora inizia l'esame?
Può dirmi a che ora inizia l'esame?
Puoi dirmi a che ora inizia l'esame?

rubric: Formal address to one person uses the Lei form, which is the third person singular: può dirmi.
Distractors use tu, voi or mix formal and informal pronouns.

items.prompt: Choose the correct form: "Maria e Lucia ___ presto ieri sera." (uscire)
rubric: Uscire takes essere in the passato prossimo, and the participle agrees with the feminine plural subject: uscite.
Distractors use avere or fail to make the participle agree.

items.prompt: Replace both objects with pronouns: "Ho dato il libro a Marco."
rubric: Indirect gli plus direct lo combine into glielo, which elides before ho: gliel'ho dato.
Distractors keep gli separate, use the wrong pronoun, or use the feminine le.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: "Domani vado ___ dentista alle tre."
rubric: Going to a person's place uses da plus the article: dal dentista.
Al is the common error, used for places rather than people.

items.prompt: Choose the correct verb form: "Leggevo un libro quando Luca ___ in camera."
rubric: A sudden interrupting action in the past uses the passato prossimo, and entrare takes essere.
Entrava treats the interruption as a background action; ha entrato uses the wrong auxiliary.

items.prompt: Complete the sentence: "Voglio che tu ___ subito." (venire)
rubric: Volere che plus a different subject requires the congiuntivo presente: venga.
Vieni and verrai use the indicative; verresti uses the conditional.

items.prompt: Which sentences are correct Italian? Select all that apply.

options.label: Non ho visto nessuno al bar.

rubric: Nessuno follows non, the partitive dello zucchero is correct, and piacere agrees with the thing liked (piacciono).
Distractors add a spurious preposition or fail to make piacere agree with a plural subject.

items.prompt: Marco is writing to the manager of a hotel he has never met and wants the manager to confirm his booking. He wants a polite, formal sentence in Italian. Which sentence should he use?

options.label: Ti sarei grato se potessi confermare la mia prenotazione.
Le sarei grato se potesse confermare la mia prenotazione.
Vi sarei grato se poteste confermare la mia prenotazione.
Le sarei grato se puoi confermare la mia prenotazione.

rubric: Formal address to one person uses Lei with a consistent third-person form: Le ... potesse.
Distractors mix registers (ti, puoi) or use the plural vi for a single person.

items.prompt: Which part contains an error? "Ieri sono andata al mercato e ho comprato delle mele, ma le ho mangiato tutte subito."
rubric: A direct object pronoun placed before avere makes the participle agree: le ho mangiate.
Sono andata is correct with essere and a feminine subject.

items.prompt: A learner writes "Mi dispiace che tu non hai capito." What is the best diagnosis?

options.label: Mi dispiace requires an infinitive after it, so non aver capito is needed.
The conjunction is wrong, so di is needed in place of che here.
Verbs of emotion plus che take the congiuntivo, so abbia capito is needed.
The action is past, so the imperfetto non capivi is needed.

rubric: Expressions of feeling like mi dispiace trigger the subjunctive in the che clause.
Other options misidentify the structure: infinitive, tense, or conjunction.

items.prompt: Which sentence misuses sapere or conoscere?
rubric: Conoscere means to be familiar with people or places; knowing a fact in a clause needs sapere: So che Luca è malato.
The other sentences use sapere for skills and information, and conoscere for places, correctly.

items.prompt: A learner writes "Ho andato a Roma" and "Sono mangiato la pizza." Which statements correctly diagnose the errors? Select all that apply.

options.label: Mangiare takes a direct object and needs avere: Ho mangiato.
Both verbs need avere because the actions are completed.
Both verbs need essere because the subject is io.
Both verbs need the imperfetto because they are past actions.
Andare is a verb of motion and needs essere: Sono andato.

rubric: The learner swapped the two auxiliaries: andare takes essere, mangiare takes avere.
Distractors apply one auxiliary or tense to both verbs, ignoring the verb type.

items.prompt: Which sentence is incorrectly formed?
rubric: With a modal, the reflexive pronoun goes either before the modal or attached to the infinitive, never both.
The other sentences place the pronoun in one of the two accepted ways.

items.prompt: Which pair of singular and plural forms with the definite article contains an error?
rubric: Words beginning with ps take lo / gli: lo psicologo, gli psicologi.
Distractors are correct uses of lo, l' and the plural forms.

items.prompt: A student writes "Sono 25 anni" and "Sono molto fame" in a message. The teacher wants to find the single underlying cause behind both mistakes. Which diagnosis fits best?

options.label: The student translates English "I am" literally, using essere where Italian uses avere.
The student applies the wrong article rules before nouns that begin with a vowel or a consonant cluster.
The student fails to make adjectives agree in gender and number with the subject of each sentence.
The student confuses the present tense of essere with its passato prossimo forms in both sentences.

rubric: Italian expresses age and hunger with avere (Ho 25 anni, Ho molta fame); both errors come from literal English transfer.
Distractors name unrelated problems that do not explain both errors.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'Maria si è lavato le mani.' Which analysis of the error is correct?

options.label: The sentence is correct, because reflexive participles stay masculine singular whatever the subject is.
The participle must agree with Maria, because after essere it agrees with the subject: 'lavata'.
The auxiliary must be avere, because the sentence contains a direct object: 'ha lavato'.
The participle must agree with le mani, because the direct object is plural, giving 'lavate'.

rubric: With essere, including reflexive verbs, the participle agrees with the subject even when a direct object such as le mani is present.
Distractors wrongly apply object agreement or assume a direct object forces avere.

items.prompt: A learner wants to say 'I'm thirsty' but says 'Ho sette.' The listener looks puzzled. What best explains the misunderstanding?

options.label: Sete needs essere, so 'Sono sete' is required and avere makes the phrase meaningless.
The final e is silent in Italian, so the listener hears 'set,' which is not a word.
The doubled t turns the word into the number seven, so the sentence means 'I have seven.'
Thirst is expressed with stare, so the learner needed 'Sto sete' instead of avere.

rubric: Single versus double consonants distinguish words: sete (thirst) and sette (seven).
Distractors invent verb-choice or silent-vowel rules; avere is correct for 'ho sete' and final vowels are pronounced.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'Sabato vado a mia zia a Torino.' What is the cause of the error in the first part?

options.label: Andare needs per before a person, so the phrase should be 'per mia zia' to show the visit.
Zia needs an article before the possessive, so the phrase should be 'alla mia zia'.
Torino needs in because it is a place, so the phrase should read 'in Torino' after the verb.
A person as destination needs da, not a, so it should be 'da mia zia'; a is used for cities.

rubric: Movement to a person's home takes da; a is used with cities and small places.
Distractors misapply in with cities, add an article, or invent per.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'Ho incontrato i psicologi e lo studente.' Which statement correctly identifies the faulty part?

options.label: 'i psicologi' is wrong, because psicologo looks feminine and the plural needs 'le'.
Both articles are wrong, because masculine nouns ending in -e or -i take l' before them.
'i psicologi' is wrong, because ps- is a cluster that takes lo and gli, so 'gli psicologi'.
'lo studente' is wrong, because words with st- take il in the singular, so 'il studente'.

rubric: Masculine nouns beginning with ps-, z-, gn- or s+consonant take lo/gli, so 'i psicologi' is wrong and 'lo studente' is right.
Distractors apply the wrong article rule to studente or misread psicologo's gender.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'Il mio fratello e la mia sorella abitano a Milano.' Which correction is most accurate?

options.label: Mio fratello e mia sorella, because singular unmodified family nouns drop the article after a possessive.
Il mio fratello e mia sorella, because only feminine kinship nouns drop the article.
I miei fratelli, because two siblings named together require a plural possessive.
Il fratello mio e la sorella mia, because possessives must follow family nouns.

rubric: Singular, unmodified kinship nouns normally take no article with mio/tuo/suo etc.
Distractors invent a gender restriction, a plural requirement or a word-order rule.

items.prompt: Which sentences contain an error in participle agreement? Select all that apply.

options.label: Marco si è lavato prima di uscire.
Ho comprato le mele e le ho mangiate.
Ho comprato le mele e le ho mangiato.

rubric: With essere the participle agrees with the subject (arrivate); with avere it agrees with a preceding direct-object pronoun (le ho mangiate).
The other two sentences apply these rules correctly.

items.prompt: A learner emails a colleague: 'Mi piace le tue idee, ma non ho tempo per realizzarli.' The colleague, who teaches Italian, says there are two separate errors in this sentence. Which diagnosis is accurate?

options.label: Piacere agrees with the speaker, so 'piaccio'; and the pronoun should stay masculine plural as a default, 'realizzarli'.
Piacere needs a subject pronoun, so 'Io piace'; and the pronoun must be singular, 'realizzarla'.
Piacere agrees with the thing liked, so 'piacciono'; and the pronoun must be feminine plural, 'realizzarle'.
Piacere is correct as it stands, since it is used impersonally; only the pronoun needs fixing to 'realizzarle'.

rubric: The thing liked is the grammatical subject of piacere (le idee piacciono), and idee is feminine plural, so the pronoun is 'le'.
Distractors treat piacere like an English 'like' verb or keep a default masculine pronoun.

items.prompt: You must email a professor you have never met to request a meeting. Criteria: formal register, polite request, clear purpose. Which message is best?

options.label: Buongiorno Professor Bianchi, voglio parlare con Lei della tesi, quindi mi riceva pure quando può e mi faccia sapere. Ciao.
Gentile Professor Bianchi, Le scrivo per chiederLe se potrebbe ricevermi per parlare della tesi. Cordiali saluti.
Gentile Professor Bianchi, vi scrivo per chiedervi se potete ricevermi per parlare della mia tesi di laurea. Distinti saluti.
Caro Professor Bianchi, ti scrivo per chiederti se puoi ricevermi per parlare della mia tesi di laurea. A presto, grazie.

rubric: Gentile, the Lei forms, the conditional and Cordiali saluti together give a formal, polite request.
Distractors use tu, an archaic plural voi for one person, or a blunt demand with a casual closing.

items.prompt: A learner wants to say 'I'll eventually call you back,' meaning 'in the end I will.' Which Italian version best conveys that meaning?
rubric: Alla fine means 'in the end'; 'eventualmente' is a false friend meaning 'possibly'.
Attualmente means 'currently' and casualmente 'by chance'.

items.prompt: A learner's recordings show she pronounces 'pala' and 'palla', 'caro' and 'carro' identically. She has 15 minutes a day. Criteria: targets this contrast, gives feedback on her own production, is realistic. Which plan is best?

options.label: Memorise word-stress rules, since stress placement determines whether a consonant is doubled in Italian words.
Practise rolling the r in isolation until it trills, since a trilled r also fixes the length of doubled consonants.
Repeat minimal pairs with a lengthened doubled consonant, then compare her recordings with a native model.
Read a long article aloud daily, focusing on overall fluency and rhythm without stopping on single sounds.

rubric: Minimal-pair practice with self-recording targets the exact contrast and provides feedback.
Distractors are unfocused, target stress, or target the trilled r, which is a different feature.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'Se avrei tempo, verrei alla festa.' Intended meaning: a present, unreal condition (I don't have time now). Which correction best keeps that meaning in standard grammar?

options.label: Se avrò tempo, verrei alla festa.
Se ho tempo, verrei alla festa.
Se avessi avuto tempo, verrei alla festa.
Se avessi tempo, verrei alla festa.

rubric: A present unreal condition takes se + imperfect subjunctive with a conditional in the main clause.
Distractors mix a real future or present condition with the conditional, or shift the condition to the past.

items.prompt: You promised to phone a friend but forgot, so the call never happened. Which apology best expresses that you were supposed to call but did not?
rubric: The imperfect 'dovevo' expresses an obligation that was not fulfilled.
'Ho dovuto' implies you had to and did call; the others refer to the present or future.

items.prompt: A learner aims for accurate written Italian. Which pieces of advice are sound? Select all that apply.

options.label: Use tu with every adult in writing to sound friendly, since Lei is generally considered cold.
Check participle agreement when a direct-object pronoun precedes avere, since l'ho vista agrees with the woman seen.
Translate each English preposition by its most common Italian equivalent, since the mapping is stable across verbs.
Learn verbs together with their prepositions, since pensare a and dipendere da do not map one-to-one onto English.

rubric: Verb-preposition pairs are not predictable from English, and participles agree with preceding direct-object pronouns.
Distractors claim a stable preposition mapping or recommend tu where Lei is the safe formal choice.

items.prompt: You rent a flat in Bologna. The heating has been broken since Monday and it is now Thursday. Your landlord, an older man you met once, writes to you with Lei. You want a technician this week. Which message best fits formal register, correct time expression and a polite but clear request?

options.label: Ciao, il riscaldamento non funziona per lunedì. Puoi mandare un tecnico questa settimana?
Buongiorno, Le scrivo perché il riscaldamento non ha funzionato da lunedì. Potrebbe mandare un tecnico entro questa settimana?
Gentile signor Rossi, il riscaldamento non funzionava da lunedì. Voglio un tecnico subito, grazie.
Buongiorno, Le scrivo perché il riscaldamento non funziona da lunedì. Potrebbe far venire un tecnico entro giovedì?

rubric: Present tense with da expresses an ongoing situation since Monday; Lei and the conditional keep the register polite, and the deadline is clear.
Distractors use tu with per, an imperfect with a blunt demand, or a passato prossimo that is wrong with da and has no deadline.

items.prompt: A learner claims the imperfetto is needed for any long action, so 'Ho vissuto a Roma per dieci anni' should become 'Vivevo a Roma per dieci anni.' Which evaluation is most accurate in standard Italian?

options.label: The original is correct, because a stated, bounded span of time takes the passato prossimo even if long.
The learner is right, because 'per' plus a time span always triggers the imperfetto for repeated states.
The learner is right, because ten years is long enough that duration requires the imperfetto.
The two forms are equal in meaning, since they differ only in formality, not in aspect.

rubric: A bounded period with a stated length is viewed as a completed whole, so the passato prossimo is used.
Distractors confuse length of time with aspect; the imperfetto marks unbounded or background actions.

items.prompt: A learner argues that 'Ti manco' is the correct way to say 'I miss you', since the speaker is the one doing the missing. Which evaluation is correct?

options.label: The learner is right, because the person who feels the absence is the subject and the verb agrees with them.
The learner is right in speech, but 'Mi manchi' is the written form because of the register difference.
The learner is wrong: 'Mi manchi' is correct because the missed person is the subject and the verb agrees with them.
The learner is wrong, because 'mancare' is reflexive here and needs 'mi manco' with the speaker as object.

rubric: Mancare works like piacere: the thing missed is the grammatical subject and the one who misses is the indirect object.
Distractors map English 'miss' directly onto Italian syntax.

items.prompt: A teacher states: 'The letters gli before a vowel are always pronounced /ʎ/, as in figlio.' Which word is a counterexample, with gli pronounced /gli/?
rubric: In 'glicine' (wisteria) the gli is read /gli/, not /ʎ/, so the rule has exceptions.
The other words all contain the /ʎ/ sound and support the rule.

items.prompt: Evaluate these statements about past participle agreement in standard Italian. Which is the most accurate?

options.label: Agreement with a preceding direct object is obligatory both after relative 'che' and with pronouns, so 'le lettere che ho scritto' is an outright error in standard Italian.
Agreement with a preceding direct object is optional after relative 'che' ('che ho scritto/scritte') but obligatory with lo/la/li/le ('Le ho scritte').
Agreement is never made after 'avere' in modern standard Italian, so 'Le ho scritto' is the only standard form and 'scritte' is archaic.
Agreement with a preceding direct object is optional both after relative 'che' and with pronouns, so 'Le ho scritto' is as acceptable as 'Le ho scritte' in careful writing.

rubric: With direct object pronouns lo/la/li/le agreement is required; with relative 'che' it is optional.
Distractors overgeneralise either obligation or optionality.

items.prompt: A learner wants to tell a new colleague they are looking forward to a trip and writes 'Sono molto eccitato per il viaggio.' Judged for natural, non-embarrassing Italian, which revision is best?

options.label: Sono molto stimolato per il viaggio.
Sono molto emozionato per il viaggio.
Sono molto agitato per il viaggio.
Sono molto esaltato per il viaggio.

rubric: 'Eccitato' is a false friend with a sexual connotation; 'emozionato' conveys excitement neutrally.
'Agitato' means anxious or restless, 'esaltato' suggests fanaticism, and 'stimolato' means physically stimulated.

items.prompt: Evaluate the following claims about conjunctions and mood in standard written Italian. Which are acceptable? Select all that apply.

options.label: 'Siccome' takes the congiuntivo: 'Siccome sia tardi, vado.'
'Prima che' takes the congiuntivo: 'Esci prima che piova.'
'Benché' takes the congiuntivo: 'Benché sia stanco, lavora.'
'Mentre' with simultaneous actions takes the congiuntivo: 'Mentre io legga, lei canta.'
'Dopo che' takes the indicativo: 'Dopo che sei partito, ha telefonato.'

rubric: Benché and prima che require the congiuntivo; dopo che takes the indicativo in standard usage.
Siccome and a simultaneous 'mentre' take the indicativo; the other two options wrongly extend subjunctive use.

items.prompt: A learner writes 'Ho corso a casa per prendere l'ombrello' and later 'Sono corso per un'ora nel parco.' A tutor wants to give the most accurate feedback on auxiliary choice with 'correre'. Which feedback is correct?

options.label: Both are wrong, because motion verbs always take 'essere' regardless of context or destination.
Swap them: 'ho corso' suits a destination, and 'sono corso' suits an activity lasting an hour.
'Sono corso a casa' with a destination, but 'ho corso per un'ora' for the activity itself.
Both are right, because 'correre' accepts either auxiliary freely with no change in meaning.

rubric: Correre takes essere when a destination or direction is expressed and avere when it is just the activity.
Distractors claim free variation, a blanket essere rule, or reverse the pattern.

items.prompt: Combine 'Ho incontrato una ragazza. Le ho prestato il libro.' into one sentence using a relative pronoun, in standard written Italian, with the indirect-object link preserved.

options.label: Ho incontrato la ragazza a cui le ho prestato il libro.
Ho incontrato la ragazza che le ho prestato il libro.
Ho incontrato la ragazza a cui ho prestato il libro.
Ho incontrato la ragazza di cui ho prestato il libro.

rubric: The indirect object needs a preposition plus relative: 'a cui' (or 'alla quale').
Distractors keep the redundant pronoun, drop the preposition, or use the wrong one.

items.prompt: Write a sentence that expresses an unreal past condition with a result that is still true now ('If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now'). Which sentence meets every constraint in standard Italian?

options.label: Se avessi studiato medicina, ora avrei essere medico.
Se studiavo medicina, ora ero medico.
Se avrei studiato medicina, ora sarei medico.
Se avessi studiato medicina, ora sarei medico.

rubric: Past unreal condition takes the trapassato congiuntivo and a present conditional result (mixed hypothetical).
Distractors use the wrong tense in the se-clause or a malformed compound conditional.

items.prompt: Rewrite 'Voglio dare il libro a Maria' replacing both objects with pronouns, attaching them to the infinitive. Which is correct in standard Italian?
rubric: Indirect 'gli/le' becomes 'glie-' before 'lo' and fuses into one word: glielo, for masculine or feminine.
Distractors keep 'le', separate the pronouns, or form non-existent combinations.

items.prompt: Report 'Verrò domani' in a past narrative in standard written Italian, shifting tense and time marker: 'Disse che ___'. Which completion meets both constraints?
rubric: Future in the past is the conditional composto, and 'domani' shifts to 'il giorno dopo'.
Distractors keep the future, use the future anterior, or leave 'domani' unshifted.

items.prompt: A Spanish speaker has 12 weeks to reach everyday conversation in Italian. Design constraints: use the learner's strengths, target likely interference, and prioritise speaking. Which plan fits best?

options.label: Study the full verb tables first, and delay speaking until all tenses are mastered in writing.
Translate Spanish texts word for word, leaving pronunciation and false friends to sort themselves out through reading.
Use cognates for fast vocabulary, drill double consonants and false friends by shadowing, run weekly role-plays.
Memorise long lists of Spanish-Italian cognates first, since the similarity makes grammar and pronunciation practice unnecessary.

rubric: The best plan leverages similarity while explicitly targeting interference such as gemination and false friends, with speaking practice.
Distractors rely on transfer without correction, delay speaking, or overload grammar.

items.prompt: Complete 'Verrò alla festa ___' so that it means 'only on condition that you come too' and uses a construction requiring the congiuntivo. Select all that apply.

options.label: dato che tu venga con me.
a condizione che tu venga con me.

rubric: 'Purché' and 'a condizione che' express condition and require the congiuntivo (venga).
The others use the indicativo where a subjunctive is needed, or add a subjunctive after se/dato che wrongly.

items.prompt: A teacher is designing a pronunciation exercise on double consonants for learners who ignore consonant length. She needs every pair to differ only in consonant length and to be two real words. Which set of pairs meets all constraints?
rubric: Only caro/carro, pala/palla and sete/sette differ solely by single versus double consonant.
Other sets include pairs differing in a vowel or consonant, such as casa/cosa or pane/cane.
